label: that-clauses: saying what somebody said or thinks
note: CLOSED by chapter 72. The note's claim was verified by token rather than by substring, which mattered here: the string `enna` DOES appear in the corpus, five times in ML-C64-but and four in ML-C69, but every one of those is inside ennaal, the word for `but` that ML-C64 teaches. The QUOTATIVE ennu -- with the virama -- appeared nowhere. THE CHAPTER TEACHES ONE MARKER AND BUYS BACK THE WHOLE CORPUS: ennu leaves the quoted sentence untouched and marks it as the thing said, so every sentence the reader can already build becomes something they can report, think, claim to know or ask. English rebuilds a reported clause and Malayalam does not, which is the comparison the lessons lead with. IT OPENS FOUR VERBS THAT WERE ALREADY TAUGHT -- parayuka, cintikkuka, ariyuka and codikkuka -- so the chapter costs two atoms and reaches four frames. THE SAYING-VERB ITSELF WAS A SEPARATE FINDING AND IS FIXED IN CHAPTER 50, NOT HERE. parayuka was never a headword anywhere, while ML-C50-farewell built `vita parayuka` and called it `the speaking-verb` because there was no name to give it, and ML-C50-journey used it too. Teaching it at chapter 72 turned those two into forward references 104 and 106 lessons early, so the lesson moved to sequence 1405 -- immediately before the first use -- which took forwardReferences back to its baseline and paid a debt that predated this work.
